overview: TPAura is a long-range kill aura that attacks the nearest visible player from the client's current position. Despite the name there is no teleportation in this build: a MotionEvent pre handler rebuilds a target list from every EntityPlayer within the Range setting (8 to 300 blocks, default 50) that canEntityBeSeen returns true for, sorts it by distance, and on a randomized 1 to 25 CPS gate (default 10) swings and sends C02PacketUseEntity ATTACK without ever changing the view direction. The two rotation modes are empty switch cases, so the attack vector is whatever position and facing the vanilla C03 stream last reported; the optional autoblock layer sends C08 (facing 255, BlockPos(-1,-1,-1)) once per block cycle and C07 RELEASE_USE_ITEM to drop it.

sections.p: The module is one MotionEvent pre listener plus an UpdateEvent suffix setter. sortAndAddTargets clears targetList and scans mc.theWorld.getLoadedEntityList each pre-motion, keeping EntityPlayer instances that are within reach, not the local player, visible to canEntityBeSeen, not invisible, and not registered as friends, then sorts by getDistanceToEntity ascending. currentTarget is the first entry and blocking is computed as autoBlock enabled with a sword held and a target present. When the list empties mid-flight the handler only releases a pending block, so the attack machinery never runs without a target.

sections.h: Attack cadence and the empty rotation modes
sections.p: The attack branch is gated by rotate and by timerUtil.hasTimeElapsed(1000 / cps, true) where cps is Math.round(MathUtil.getRandomInRange(minimumCPS, maximumCps)) re-rolled on every fire, so each interval is a fresh random value between 40ms at 25 CPS and 1000ms at 1 CPS. Both rotationMode cases ("Nope lol" and "Not needed") are empty switch branches and no yaw or pitch write exists anywhere in the file, so the module attacks with the player's actual view. swingItem and addToSendQueue(C02 ATTACK) are the whole send path; the enchantParticle and criticalParticle settings call onEnchantmentCritical and onCriticalHit, which are client-side visual effects only.

The autoblock state machine is a wasBlocked latch. Vanilla mode sends one C08(new BlockPos(-1,-1,-1), 255, heldItem, 0, 0, 0) when the latch flips, Hurt Time mode waits for hurtTime == 9, and the release C07 (RELEASE_USE_ITEM at BlockPos.ORIGIN, DOWN) fires when hurtTime returns to 0, when the target list empties, or in onDisable. The C02 attacks therefore arrive from the position the vanilla C03 movement stream reports; at default range 50 the server measures hits roughly 50 blocks from the victim with no rotation change preceding them, which is the whole detection surface.

files.label: TPAura.java (module)
files.explanation: The module is the onMotionEvent listener plus the target-sorting helper. sortAndAddTargets filters the loaded entity list by range, visibility, invisibility and friend status and sorts by distance, currentTarget is the nearest survivor, and the pre-motion branch runs the CPS gate, the swing, the C02 send, and the autoblock latch. onDisable releases a pending block and clears both targetList and the blocking flags. The two rotationMode cases are empty, which is the key finding: the Rotate toggle gates the attack loop but no mode ever writes yaw or pitch, so the attacks go out with the unmodified view.

files.label: TimerUtil.java (CPS gate)
files.explanation: TimerUtil is a millisecond gate: hasTimeElapsed(time, reset) returns true once System.currentTimeMillis() minus lastMS exceeds time and, when reset is true, re-arms lastMS. The module calls it with 1000 / cps and reset true on every fire, so the gate re-arms immediately after each attack and the next interval is a fresh roll of the random CPS. This per-fire re-roll is what makes the attack stream irregular rather than a fixed metronome, which matters for the countering story: the cadence variance is the only human-like quality the module has.

countering.label: NCP fight Reach (survival distance limit)
countering.explanation: NCP fight Reach measures the attack distance from the server-tracked player position to the victim at the moment the C02 is processed. The survival distance limit in this tree is 4.02 (DefaultConfig line 366) with a reachMod reduce band between 3.22 and 4.02 that silently cancels repeat hits instead of flagging. The module attacks from its own position with no teleport assistance, so a default-range hit measures roughly 46 blocks over the limit and the violation fires on the first attack. The honest both-sides point: unlike teleport-based TP auras there is no C04 stream to revert, so the reach measurement is against the true position every time.

countering.label: Hawk EntityInteractReach (interaction distance)
countering.explanation: Hawk EntityInteractReach enforces a 3.1 block interaction limit with lag compensation enabled by default, scoring each C02 against the attacker's position history. Because the module never emits a teleport, the history is the honest vanilla movement stream and no extrapolation or rewind can bring a 50-block default hit into range; every attack flags immediately. The same distance applies to the autoblock C08 placement, which travels with the same absurd separation when the module is used at long range.

countering.label: Hawk EntityInteractDirection (facing cone ray)
countering.explanation: EntityInteractDirection expands the player hitbox by 0.2 and ray traces from the server-observed yaw and pitch to the target; a hit outside the facing cone fails. The module never rotates, so the server-observed facing is whatever the player last moved with, and every victim off that cone fails direction regardless of distance. Only targets standing inside the current facing cone pass, which makes the check a second independent filter on top of the reach checks.

countering.label: NCP fight Angle (attack stream rotation)
countering.explanation: NCP fight Angle scores the attack stream inside a 1000ms window with angleVL accumulation and a 0.98 decay, testing how much the player moved, how fast attacks follow each other, how far yaw changes between attacks, and how often the target switches. The module maximizes every signal: zero yaw change, sub-50ms gaps at high CPS, and nearest-first target switches with no turn. At the stock thresholds in this tree (move 100, time 150, yaw 60, switch 50) per-call scores cap at 20 to 30 and never trip, so the check is dormant until an admin lowers the thresholds; on detection configs the same stream flags immediately.
